title: Waitangi Treaty Grounds Family Review: What Kids Really Experience
meta_desc: Honest family review of Waitangi Treaty Grounds – cost, kid‑friendliness, best time to go, booking tricks and drawbacks, so parents can plan a Bay of Islands day.
intro: The Waitangi Treaty Grounds are a must‑see on a Bay of Islands road‑trip, but how does a day out with kids really feel? We break down the experience, costs and practical tips for families.

sections.heading: What to Expect
sections.body:
When you pull into the car park (free for the first 30 minutes, then $5/hr), you’re greeted by the iconic flag‑pole and the historic flagstaff where the Treaty was signed. The main visitor centre opens at 9 am; a short walk leads to the performance arena and the museum.

The daily Maori cultural performance runs every hour from 10 am to 3 pm and lasts about 30 minutes. It’s a vivid showcase of haka, waiata and traditional weaponry that holds children’s attention – especially if you sit close to the front.

After the show, the museum’s interactive displays let kids trace the Treaty’s story with touch‑screens and replica artifacts. Most families spend 2–3 hours here before heading out to explore the surrounding bays.
list: Free parking for the first 30 min, then $5 per hour
Museum open 9 am‑5 pm (last entry 4:30 pm)
